prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single “AI recommendation checker.” The best practical approach is to (a) make sure your business is listed and structured where AI systems pull data from (Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, Wikipedia/Wikidata), (b) use a local-listing/citation management tool to audit/sync those sources, and (c) test live LLMs and search-powered chatbots directly.

Concrete steps and recommended services

1) Start with the essentials (free, highest impact)
- Google Business Profile (GBP): claim and fully fill out your profile. Google data is used by many services and influences AI-driven recommendations.
- Bing Places, Apple Maps / Apple Business Connect, Yelp, Facebook Business: claim and complete these as well.

2) Use a listings/citation manager to check and sync presence across many sources
- Yext — enterprise-grade: syncs data to many publishers and markets itself as powering knowledge for AI and assistants.
- BrightLocal — local SEO audits, citation checks, rank tracking and review monitoring.
- Moz Local, Whitespark, Semrush Listing Management — good alternatives for citation/finding visibility gaps.

3) Publish structured data and authoritative references
- Add Schema.org (LocalBusiness) markup on your website and ensure NAP (name, address, phone) is consistent across sites.
- Get a Wikidata entry and, if appropriate, a Wikipedia page or high-quality press mentions — these feed knowledge graphs that AIs use.

4) Test AI engines directly
- Ask multiple models (ChatGPT, Bard, Bing Chat, Perplexity, Copilot) with local-aware prompts and request sources. Example prompts:
  - “Recommend a [type of business] near [city or zip code]. Please list sources or links.”
  - “Do you know [My Business Name] in [City]? If so, why would you recommend it—what sources are you using?”
- Run these tests a few times (answers vary) and note whether the assistant cites Google, Yelp, news articles, or nothing.

5) Programmatic / monitoring options
- Use Google Maps Platform API / Bing Maps API to verify your place IDs and presence programmatically.
- Use BrightLocal / Semrush for ongoing rank tracking and report generation.

Why this combination?
- No single tool can tell you all LLM recommendations because models use varied data sources (search indexes, knowledge graphs, proprietary datasets). Ensuring authoritative, consistent listings and structured data gives the best chance LLMs will return or cite your business. Listing managers (Yext/BrightLocal) save time and give visibility reports; direct prompts to LLMs reveal what each engine currently “knows.”

If you’d like, I can:
- Run a short test prompt against major chatbots for your business (need business name + city/zip), or
- Audit the top listings and give a prioritized checklist of things to fix. Which would you prefer?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
